archetypes.name: loop-status-completeness
archetypes.rationale: The plan enumerates only a subset of LOOP_STATUS values in the bypass list; panel-failed, main-agent-vote-required, and cap-reached (vs cap-hit) need explicit routing coverage.
archetypes.prompt_body: Audit every LOOP_STATUS token emitted by plan-review-loop.sh against the routing branches documented in SKILL.md Step 3 and approval-gates.md Gate B. Identify any status value that is produced by the script but has no explicit routing rule in the prose — meaning the orchestrator may fall through to an unintended path (e.g. auto-apply when it should bypass, or silent skip of Step 3.6 when it should run). Pay particular attention to panel-failed, main-agent-vote-required, zero-findings-degraded-panel, and cap-hit vs cap-reached token discrepancies. Also check whether the plan's proposed prose additions to SKILL.md and approval-gates.md cover every missing status or only the three named in the issue. Cite specific file paths and line ranges for any issues found, and follow the output-format rules from your outer wrapper exactly.

archetypes.name: test-isolation-fidelity
archetypes.rationale: The proposed integration test claims to invoke real snapshot-plan-round.sh and assess-plan-round.sh, but the harness exclusively uses mock stubs; verifying whether real scripts are actually exercised is plan-critical.
archetypes.prompt_body: Examine the proposed integration test case in test-assess-plan-round.sh for the cursor-advance to Gate B settle to write-after to second Step 3 entry scenario. Determine whether the new case would use the real snapshot-plan-round.sh and assess-plan-round.sh binaries or whether it inherits the mock-dispatch and mock-monitor stubs already set by earlier test cases in the same file. Check whether test isolation between cases (stub reset, artifact reset) is enforced so later cases cannot inherit state from earlier ones. Also verify whether the harness currently exercises the write-after subcommand of snapshot-plan-round.sh at all, or only the read-cursor and write-original subcommands. Cite specific file paths and line ranges for any issues found, and follow the output-format rules from your outer wrapper exactly.
